doc.title: Authorization
doc.paragraph: This chapter describes how an application decides whether a request may access a resource: the application's authorization control and the authorization handlers that take part in each decision. The Authorization chapter of the Architecture Guide explains the model behind it.

section.title: How a Decision Is Made
section.paragraph: Each check asks whether an action may be performed on a resource. The resource is a path such as /objects/Note/n1, or /afw/_AdaptiveFunction_/service_restart for a function call. The action is one of create, read, query, modify, delete and execute.

steps.step: The application's initialAuthorizationCheck runs first, if there is one. A result of permit or deny is the final decision.
Otherwise each running authorization handler is asked, in priority order, and their decisions are combined.
If the final result is still notApplicable, access is permitted, unless the application's denyIfNotApplicable is true.

section.paragraph: Checks apply to requests from clients (user mode) and, when checkIntermediateMode is true, to the accesses a model adapter makes on a client's behalf. Code running in core mode is checked only by coreAuthorizationCheck, if one is given. A denied request fails with error denied, for example Access 'delete' to '/objects/Note/n1' is not permitted.

section.title: Authorization Control
section.paragraph: The application entry's authorizationControl property controls checking for the whole application:

A check script returns an object whose decisionId is permit, deny or notApplicable. While it runs, current::actionId, current::resourceId, current::object (the object, or for execute the function and its arguments, when there is one) and current::requestId describe the access, and request properties such as request::REMOTE_ADDR are available.

section.title: Authorization Handlers
section.paragraph: An authorizationHandler entry adds a handler, identified by authorizationHandlerId, of the type named by authorizationHandlerType. A handler is a service named authorizationHandler- followed by its id. These properties are common to every handler:

A handler's decision does not replace an earlier handler's permit or deny unless allowDenyOverride or allowPermitOverride says it may. A required handler that is not running makes checks fail rather than skip it.

section.title: Script
section.paragraph: The script handler, provided by core, decides by running the Adaptive Script in authorizationCheck, with the same current:: variables and result as the application's check scripts.
This handler refuses deletes in the adapter objects and has no opinion on anything else:
Values in qualifiedVariables are available to the script under their qualifier, which keeps lists such as allowed users out of the script text.
